newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia govt says to sell AN through tender.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia govt says to sell AN through tender.

text.p: The Australian government said on Thursday it would take immediate steps to sell rail operator Australian National through competitive tender.

It said the decision resulted from the government's scoping study into Australian National, which operates workshops and freight and passengers services, and interstate freight operator National Rail Corp, which had found significant investor interest in both companies.

"The scoping study into the sale of Australian National (AN) and the Commonwealth's interest in National Rail (NR) identified considerable market interest in the sale and accordingly, the government has decided to take immediate steps to offer AN for sale by competitive tender," the government said in a statement.

Transport Minister John Sharp said buyers would be able to bid for the whole of AN's intrastate operations or for the component parts. Rolling stock and intrastate track would be offered as part of the sale, he said.
"Our intention is to maximise private sector involvement to ensure the long time viability of -- and growth in -- the industry," Sharp said.
AN is fully owned by the government and operates freight services and workshops in South Australia and Tasmania, together with three interstate passenger services.
